reason: The rule file's own example syntax: an example fixes a function's result by writing "fn()" as a key.
now is the reply key holding the stat at the gene's own value; the text names the key, not a change.
The undo_refused error says a job an earlier undo took back cannot be undone: was names the state it is in, not a past change to the mod.
The undo_refused error says the world may have moved on since the job ran: changed compares the world now with the job's own record, not a change to the mod.
The undo_refused error lists what a diverged world looks like (a thing the job built gone or another prefab): changed is that case, not a change to the mod.
since relates the world now to the moment the job ran (the undo's own check), not a version of the mod.
The queue_full error says the call added nothing to a full job queue: was queued is that call's own outcome, not a change to the mod.
